query: What happens if adhesion is not done correctly during socket fabrication?
context: - ABS: Not recommended. Releases styrene vapors during printing. Poor layer adhesion and warping in humid environments like Punjab. - TPU (flexible): Safe for liner applications. Shore hardness 95A is standard for prosthetic liners. Always print in a ventilated space. Install a HEPA filter enclosure on the printer if available. 6. Post-Processing Steps -------------------------- After printing a socket, follow these steps before fitting: Step 1 – Inspection: - Check all layer lines for delamination (visible gaps between layers). - Use a strong flashlight held at a tangent angle to the surface to reveal defects. - Reject any socket with visible delamination. Do not attempt to repair with glue. Step 2 – Sanding: - Inner surface: Sand with 120 grit (rough), then 220 grit, then 400 grit. - Outer surface: Sand with 220 grit only for cosmetic finish. - Wear N95 mask during sanding to avoid inhaling fine plastic dust. Step 3 – Edge Finishing: - Trim proximal and distal edges with a Dremel rotary tool or sharp knife. - Smooth all edges with a heat gun at low setting to remove sharp burrs. - A sharp socket edge will lacerate skin. Do not skip this step. Step 4 – Test Fitting: - Check socket on a solid model or foam replica of the residual limb (same circumference) before patient fitting. - Socket should slide onto model with moderate hand pressure but not fall off under gravity. 7. Failure Modes and Troubleshooting --------------------------------------- Common 3D-printed socket failures and their causes: | Failure | Cause | Prevention | |---|---|---| | Layer delamination | Low print temperature, high cooling, wet filament | Dry filament 4h at 65°C, increase temp by 5°C | | Warping | Poor bed adhesion | Use PEI bed, brim, bed at 80°C | | Stringing | Too high print temperature | Reduce by 5°C, enable retraction | | Under-extrusion | Partial nozzle clog | Cold pull cleaning | | Socket cracks at trim line | Stress concentration, too thin wall | Increase perimeters, add fillet at trim line | 8. Filament Storage -------------------- PETG absorbs moisture from humid air (Punjab's humidity can reach 80%+). Moist filament causes: - Bubbling and popping during printing - Poor layer adhesion - Rough surface finish - Reduced tensile strength Store filament in sealed containers with silica gel desiccant. Before using a new roll, dry PETG in an oven at 65°C for 4 hours. Do not exceed 70°C or the filament will soften in the tube. 9. Maintenance Schedule for Clinic Printer -------------------------------------------- A prosthetics clinic printer must be maintained regularly to ensure dimensional accuracy: - Weekly: Level the print bed using a 0.1 mm feeler gauge or auto-leveling routine. - Monthly: Clean the nozzle with a cold pull (nylon filament at 90°C). Lubricate Z-axis lead screw with PTFE grease. - Quarterly: Replace the nozzle (brass nozzle wears with abrasive filaments). Check belt tension. - Annually: Replace the print bed surface and Bowden tube (if applicable). Dimensional accuracy requirement for prosthetic sockets: ±0.5 mm.
